item.title: National Revolution and Solidarity Day to be observed Saturday
item.description:
The country is set to observe the National Revolution and Solidarity Day on Saturday commemorating the 51st anniversary of the historic events of November 7, 1975.
On the eve of the day, President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman issued separate messages.
The government has taken an elaborate program to mark the day as it has been announced a public holiday.
As part of the program, national flag will be hoisted atop all government, semi-government, autonomous, private buildings and educational institutions across the country as well as Bangladesh missions abroad. Major roads and road islands will be decorated with national flags.
The program includes discussions at district and upazila levels, children's drawing competitions, special broadcasting of the Nov-7, 1975 programs on state-run television and radio channels as well as private broadcasters and cultural events to be organized by Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy.
The Armed Forces will also arrange programs, including a colorful display at the Army Stadium in Dhaka.
Special prayers and munajat will be offered at mosques across the country at convenient times, seeking peace, prosperity and progress for the nation.
Special prayers will also be held at temples, churches, pagodas and other places of worship.
Improved diets will be served at hospitals, prisons, orphanages, child centres, Shishu Paribars, Shishu Sadans, juvenile correction centers, Shanti Nibash facilities and institutions for vagrants at convenient times.
All children's parks across the country will remain open free of charge throughout the day under the management of city corporations and municipalities.
Special discussions and essay competitions will also be arranged at educational institutions.
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting will arrange the publication of special articles, literary supplements and special supplements in national dailies.
Documentary films will also be screened at cinema halls and through mobile vans. Football matches will also be arranged at district headquarters and upazilas.
A special commemorative discussion will be held with the participation of families of martyred freedom fighters, war-wounded freedom fighters and valiant freedom fighters.
A colorful display will be staged at the Army Stadium in Dhaka under the supervision of the Bangladesh Cadet Corps.
The Dhaka Elevated Expressway will remain toll-free for all vehicles for six hours tomorrow on the occasion of National Revolution and Solidarity Day.
The toll waiver will remain effective from 6am to 12noon, allowing vehicles to use the expressway without paying any toll during the period.
Ruling BNP has also taken a seven-day program from November 5 to 11 to observe the day. As part of the programs, national and party flags will be hoisted at 6 am on November 7 at the BNP central office and party offices across the country.
At 11 am the same day, BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman along with national leaders and party activists, will place wreaths at the graves of Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia.
The party will bring out a colorful rally from in front of its central office in Naya Paltan at 3 pm on November 7.
District and metropolitan-level rallies will also be organized across the country that day, while rallies will be held at thana and upazila levels on November 8.
BNP and its affiliated organizations will also arrange discussion meetings and other programs marking the occasion.
Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal will hold a discussion meeting on November 5, while Jubo Dal will organize one on November 10. Krishak Dal will arrange a discussion meeting at 11 am on November 9, and JASAS will hold a discussion meeting and cultural program at 3 pm the same day.
Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal will organize a photography exhibition at Dhaka University campus at 11 am on November 7, followed by a discussion meeting on November 8. Olama Dal will distribute educational materials among orphan students.
The BNP has called upon its leaders and activists at all levels to work together to ensure the successful implementation of the programs marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day.

item.title: PM: Nov 7 spirit should guide building future Bangladesh
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for embracing the spirit of the November 7, 1975 revolution as a guiding force for building a self-reliant, democratic and welfare-oriented Bangladesh.
In a message marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day, to be observed on Saturday, the prime minister said soldiers and civilians had united on November 7, 1975 to thwart conspiracies against the country's independence and sovereignty.
Describing the day as a defining moment in the nation's history, he said it was important neither to remain trapped in the past nor to ignore historical lessons while shaping the future.
Tarique said those seeking to turn Bangladesh into a subservient state, deprive people of their democratic and political rights, establish one-party rule and undermine the armed forces had been defeated through the uprising.
However, he alleged that the defeated forces later regrouped under the Grand Alliance and, through a prolonged conspiracy, turned the country into a subservient state.
He also accused them of undermining the armed forces through the planned massacre of military personnel at the BDR headquarters in Pilkhana and establishing an authoritarian regime by denying people their voting rights and democratic freedoms.
The prime minister said the country was eventually freed from fascism through the 2024 mass uprising, led by students and people at the cost of thousands of lives.
“The War of 1971 was fought to achieve independence. The struggle of 2024 was to safeguard the independence of the country and its people,” he said.
He drew parallels between the 1975 revolution and the 2024 uprising, saying both reflected people's determination to protect the country's sovereignty and freedom.
Tarique said ensuring that no one could again deprive citizens of their rights or turn Bangladesh into a subservient state should be the foremost commitment on this year's November 7.
He stressed that national unity was essential to achieving this goal.
Referring to the Liberation War of 1971, the anti-autocracy movement of 1990 and the mass uprising of 2024, he said these historic struggles shared a common aspiration: building an independent, self-reliant and secure Bangladesh while ensuring people's democratic and political rights.
Concluding his message, the prime minister called for the patriotic and democracy-loving people to uphold the slogan: “Neither Delhi nor Pindi, nor any other country; Bangladesh comes first.”
He also wished success to all programmes organised across the country to mark the day.

item.title: Teknaf soldier attack: Titas laid to rest in Faridpur
item.description:
The body of army personnel Titas Sheikh, who was killed in a gun attack by hill-based criminals in Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar, was flown to his hometown in Nagarkanda, Faridpur, by an army helicopter on Friday.
The helicopter carrying his body landed at the Government Mahendra Narayan Academy ground in the upazila at around 4:45pm. The army later accorded him a guard of honour.
His body was then taken to the field of Atikur Rahman High School in his village, where his namaz-e-janaza was held after Maghrib prayers. He was later buried at the family graveyard.
Titas was critically injured on Thursday during a joint forces operation against a human trafficking gang in Teknaf when armed criminals opened fire from the hills. He later died while undergoing treatment at Ramu Combined Military Hospital.
His death plunged his family home in Laskardia village of Nagarkanda into mourning. His mother was left speechless by the loss of her son, while his wife and other relatives broke down in tears.

item.title: Businessman shot in broad daylight in Cox’s Bazar
item.description:
A businessman was shot in broad daylight after six armed assailants riding three motorcycles intercepted his microbus in Cox’s Bazar on Friday afternoon.
The attack took place around 3pm in front of Kharulia Lal Golap Community Centre in Sadar upazila, said Cox’s Bazar Sadar Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Sheikh Mohammad Ali.
The victim, Mahmudul Haque, 45, was initially taken to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital before being referred to Chittagong in critical condition.
Recounting the incident, Mahmudul said he was travelling from his home towards Ramu in a private microbus when six men on three motorcycles blocked his vehicle.
The assailants fired three shots at him. One of them also attempted to shoot him in the head, but the firearm failed to discharge. Mahmudul managed to escape by running from the scene. He claimed to have recognised four of the attackers as Zayed, Kitab Ali, Wazed Ali and Abu Naser, all from the Link Road area.
Mahmudul alleged that the attackers were followers of the president and general secretary of the local union BNP unit.
His family members also alleged that locals detained Abu Naser after the attack, but Jhilongja Union BNP President Rashed Ullah secured his release.
Monir, a relative of Mahmudul, alleged that the attack was orchestrated at the instigation of Liaquat Ali, a Jhilongja Union Parishad member and general secretary of the union BNP unit.
Repeated attempts to contact Rashed Ullah for his comments on the allegations were unsuccessful, as he disconnected the calls.
‘Police have been investigating the incident and efforts are underway to arrest those involved,’ OC Sheikh Mohammad Ali said.
Asked about the alleged involvement of BNP leaders, he said police were looking into the matter and collecting the victim's statement.

item.title: Three-day district-level Ijtema begins in Moulvibazar
item.description:
A three-day regional Ijtema began in Moulvibazar on Friday, bringing together thousands of devotees for religious discussions, sermons, and prayers.
Organized by the Moulvibazar district markaz of Tabligh Jamaat, the gathering is being held at its own ground near the district police lines in the town.
From early Friday morning, thousands of Muslim devotees from different upazilas of Moulvibazar and neighbouring areas began arriving in groups to attend the event. Participants are listening to religious sermons by prominent Islamic scholars from home and abroad and taking part in prayers and zikr.
Local lawmaker from Moulvibazar-3 and chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Land, M Nasser Rahman, also attended the large Jummah congregation at the Ijtema ground.
Organizers said that the gathering was part of a religious outreach initiative that began nearly 100 years ago at the Nizamuddin Banglawali Mosque in Delhi of India, under Maulana Muhammad Ilyas (RA), inspired by the teachings and practices of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his companions.
They said that the initiative aims to promote religious values among the people across the world.
Moulvibazar district Tabligh Jamaat Amir Md Abdul Hai and local members have sought cooperation from people of all walks of life to ensure the successful completion of the event.
Special security arrangements have been made by law enforcement agencies to ensure the safety and convenience of participants, as well as smooth traffic and movement around the venue.
The Ijtema will conclude on Sunday with the Akheri Munajat, a concluding prayer seeking peace, prosperity, and overall well-being for the country, the nation, and the Muslim Ummah.

item.title: Tahsif murder case: Disha sent to jail after remand
item.description:
Jerika Tasnim Disha, a friend of former air force officer Tahsif Sauri, was sent to jail on Friday after completing two rounds of remand in a murder case filed over his death.
Investigation Officer Inspector Firoz Uddin of the Tongi River Police Outpost produced Disha before the court and sought her detention in jail, saying she had provided important information during questioning.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid ordered her to be sent to jail. Prosecution Sub-Inspector Saiful Islam confirmed the development, adding that no bail petition had been filed on her behalf.
In the detention petition, the investigation officer said Disha had told investigators that she went to Nest Bar and Restaurant in Uttara with Tahsif on the night of October 27. She also said they had visited CP Five Star Snacks several times that evening and travelled together on Tahsif’s motorcycle.
The officer said Disha had provided several important details about the incident, which were being kept confidential pending verification. However, she allegedly avoided answering several questions and remained silent during parts of the interrogation.
Investigators also cross-checked her statements with those of another suspect, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip, who is currently on remand. A review of Tahsif’s phone records also showed that he had spoken to Disha several times, the petition said.
The investigation has so far found preliminary evidence suggesting Disha’s involvement, the officer said, adding that further investigation was underway. He argued that she needed to remain in custody to prevent her from fleeing or obstructing the investigation.
Disha was arrested in the Kafrul area last Saturday. A court initially placed her on a four-day remand on Sunday and granted a further three days on Wednesday.
Dip has also been questioned in several rounds of remand.
Tahsif’s body was recovered by river police from the Rajabari Ghat area of the Turag River on the afternoon of October 28. He had left home on his motorcycle on the evening of October 27 after being called by Dip.
Dip was arrested after Tahsif’s father filed a murder case on the night of October 30. Police later recovered Tahsif’s motorcycle from the Mazar slum area of Tongi, based on information provided by Dip.

item.title: Home Science College students continue protest over principal’s resignation
item.description:
Students of Government College of Applied Human Science in Dhaka continued their protest for a 2nd consecutive day on Friday, demanding the resignation of the principal and a fair investigation into an alleged police attack on students.
The protesters blocked the road in front of the college from Friday morning, maintaining their 72-hour ultimatum over their 2-point demands. They said they would continue their sit-in until the demands were met.
The students initially gathered inside the college premises after 9am before moving to the road, taking into consideration candidates sitting for a scheduled government job examination. The blockade brought traffic on both sides of the road to a halt.
Protesting students said participation was relatively low on Friday as the campus was closed, but more students would join the movement when it reopened on Saturday.
Student protester Seema Akter said: “We remain firm on our 2 demands. Not just 72 hours, we will stay here until our demands are met. The number of students appears low today because the campus is closed. More students will join from tomorrow when the campus reopens. Those of us who are here will remain steadfast in our demands.”
The students' 2-point demands include the resignation of college principal Professor Meherunnesa. They have demanded that all classes and examinations remain suspended and that she be barred from entering the campus until she submits a written declaration of resignation.
Their second demand is a fair investigation into the alleged police operation at the college and its female students' residential hall at midnight, during which students claim they were beaten with batons. They have also demanded justice for the police personnel involved and an update on the investigation within 72 hours.
The latest protest follows demonstrations that began on Thursday, when students staged a sit-in outside the principal's office at around 10:30am and later confined her there.
Police went to the college at around 11:30pm and rescued the principal. The protesters alleged that police baton-charged students during the operation, leaving several injured.
Following the incident, students continued their demonstration on the road in front of the college late Thursday night. They later held a press conference, demanding the principal's resignation and justice over the alleged police assault, while setting a 72-hour deadline for the implementation of their demands.
Regarding reports of injuries during the police operation, Seema Akter said: “Three to 4 people are in hospital due to baton injuries. Many girls were hit with batons. Besides, some were dragged down by their hair, while others were pulled down by their hands. We have videos and photographs of these incidents. I was also at the scene and went live on Facebook.”
Meanwhile, Lalbagh police station Officer-in-Charge Jamil Hossain said some students had blocked the road in front of the college on Friday. He said police would not obstruct them as long as they continued their program peacefully.
Regarding Thursday night's incident, Jamil said police had faced resistance from students while trying to rescue the principal. However, he denied that police had used force during the operation.
The dispute began over the cancellation of 2 residential hall seats and a Tk12,600 fine imposed on 2 students who organized a farewell program at the college auditorium before the Puja holidays.
According to students and college administration sources, postgraduate final-year students from 5 departments across 3 residential halls organized the program.
The event was initially scheduled to end by 10pm, but the deadline was extended until midnight following a request from students. However, the program continued until 5am.
Citing the use of the auditorium beyond the permitted time, principal Meherunnesa cancelled the residential hall seats of the 2 students who coordinated the event.
The students alleged that when they later approached the principal to apologize and seek reinstatement of their seats, they were asked to pay Tk12,600 to cover the auditorium's air-conditioning and electricity bills for one night.
The students subsequently launched their protest over the decision.
However, Professor Meherunnesa denied the students' allegations while speaking to journalists on Thursday. She said the students had been permitted to hold the program until midnight but continued it until 5am.
She said the residential hall seats of the 2 students had been cancelled for exceeding the permitted time. She added that she later became lenient after they apologized but decided to collect the electricity bill to maintain discipline.

item.title: Three bodies found in Teknaf hills amid ongoing joint operation
item.description:
Law enforcement agencies have received information about three bodies lying in the remote hills of Hnila union in Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar, and are making efforts to recover them.
Joint forces operations in the area are continuing following the killing of an army soldier during a gunfight with an armed human trafficking syndicate.
Police received information about the bodies in the hills between Nayapara and Leda Rohingya camps on Friday afternoon.
Cox’s Bazar Superintendent of Police ANM Sajedur Rahman confirmed the matter, saying they had received reports of three bodies in the hills.
“Efforts are underway to recover the bodies, while operations by law enforcement agencies are continuing in the area,” he said.
On Thursday afternoon, a gunfight broke out during a joint forces raid on an armed human trafficking syndicate’s hideout in the hills. Army soldier Titas Sheikh, 27, was killed after being shot by members of the syndicate.
During the operation, the joint forces rescued 56 people and detained six suspected members of the trafficking syndicate. The rescued individuals were handed over to Teknaf Model Police Station on Friday morning.
Expressing deep sorrow over the soldier’s death, the police superintendent said: “We are deeply saddened and shocked by the death of an army soldier who was shot by armed human traffickers while performing his duties.”
He stressed that eliminating such criminal activities required collective efforts from law enforcement agencies and local residents.

item.title: Winter vegetables bring relief, fish, meat and egg prices remain high
item.description:
The arrival of early winter vegetables has brought some relief to shoppers in Dhaka, with increased supplies pushing down the prices of beans, cauliflower, cabbage and radish. However, tomatoes, green chillies, carrots and round eggplants remain expensive, while fish, meat and egg prices have largely remained unchanged.
A visit to several kitchen markets in the capital on Friday found that most fish and meat items were selling at prices similar to those of the previous week.
Beans were selling for Tk60–80 per kg, while cauliflower cost Tk40–50 apiece and cabbage Tk50–60. Radish was priced at Tk40–60 per kg. Ridge gourd, sponge gourd and taro were selling for around Tk60 per kg.
Eggplant prices ranged from Tk40 to Tk70 per kg depending on variety and size, while round eggplants cost as much as Tk120.
Among the costlier vegetables, tomatoes and green chillies were selling for Tk120 per kg, while carrots cost Tk140. Local cucumbers were priced at Tk80 per kg and hybrid varieties at Tk60.
Okra and taro stems were selling for Tk50–60 per kg, while yardlong beans, bitter gourd and spiny gourd cost Tk60–80. Bottle gourds were priced at Tk40–50 each, papaya at Tk30 and sweet pumpkins at Tk30–40. Potatoes were selling for Tk25–30 per kg.
There was little change in the fish market, with most varieties selling at prices close to last week's rates.
Depending on size, rohu was selling for Tk280–380 per kg, large tilapia and silver and grass carp for Tk180–200, and pangas for Tk160–250.
Katla was priced at Tk350–380 per kg, farmed koi at Tk200–220 and pabda at Tk380–420.
Ilish remained beyond the reach of many consumers, selling for Tk800–2,300 per kg depending on size and quality. Large fish were priced as high as Tk2,600 per kg in some markets.
Meat prices also remained largely stable. Broiler chicken was selling for Tk180–190 per kg, while Sonali chicken cost Tk310–330. Beef was priced at Tk800–850 per kg and mutton at Tk1,200–1,250.
Egg prices offered little relief either, with a dozen brown eggs selling for Tk145–150 and white eggs for Tk130–135.
Mehedi, a vegetable seller at Ray Saheb Bazar, said supplies of winter vegetables had increased over the past few days, bringing down the prices of some items.
“Not all winter vegetables have arrived in sufficient quantities yet. Prices may fall further as supplies increase,” he said.
Shopper Nur Nabi said the arrival of seasonal vegetables had brought some relief, but several items remained expensive.
“Prices have come down a little, but fish, meat and eggs are still costly. People would feel much more relieved if their prices also fell,” he said.
Despite the improved supply of seasonal vegetables, high prices of fish, meat and eggs continue to put pressure on household budgets, particularly for low-income consumers.

item.title: ‘Joy Bangla’, names of 4 national leaders dropped from Coast Guard ships
item.description:
The Bangladesh Coast Guard has renamed 5 of its ships, dropping the name Joy Bangla and those of 4 national leaders, following approval from the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Under the approved changes, BCGS Joy Bangla has been renamed BCGS Adommo Bangla. The 4 vessels previously named after national leaders have also been given new names.
The 4 other vessels have been renamed as follows: BCGS Syed Nazrul to BCGS Firoz Kabir, BCGS Tajuddin to BCGS Nurul Islam, BCGS Mansur Ali to BCGS M Humayun Kabir, and BCGS Kamruzzaman to BCGS Ashraf Siddiqui.
A letter conveying the approval was sent to the director general of the Bangladesh Coast Guard by the ministry’s Border-3 Branch last Thursday.
According to the letter, the ministry approved the renaming following a proposal submitted by the Bangladesh Coast Guard.
The letter stated that the changes had received approval from the appropriate authority. It was signed by Masfika Hossain, senior assistant secretary of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
However, the letter did not specify the reasons for the renaming or the basis for selecting the new names.

item.title: 56 rescued from human traffickers’ hideout in Teknaf handed over to police
item.description:
The joint forces have handed over 56 people rescued from an armed human trafficking syndicate’s hideout in the remote hills of Rongikhali in Teknaf’s Hnila union of Cox’s Bazar to police.
They were handed over to Teknaf Model Police Station on Friday morning.
Meanwhile, the killing of an army soldier by armed human traffickers during a joint forces operation has triggered anger and concern among local residents.
Locals and public representatives have demanded a sweeping operation to dismantle the traffickers’ hideouts across the hills.
Student representatives have also called for human chains at different locations in Teknaf after Friday prayers to protest the incident.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), a gunfight broke out on Thursday afternoon during a joint forces operation against human traffickers in the remote hills of Rongikhali.
Army soldier Titas Sheikh, 27, was killed after being shot by armed traffickers during the operation. Five members of the trafficking gang were arrested, and a pistol, a locally made firearm and four rounds of ammunition were recovered.
Personnel from the Army’s 10 Infantry Division, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) and police took part in the operation.
Teknaf Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Saiful Islam said the 56 rescued people had been handed over to police, who were verifying their identities and other details.
Legal proceedings were also underway over the killing of the army soldier, he added.
The OC said police had been informed about plans to organise human chains demanding action against the criminals.
Asaduzzaman, a resident of Faridpur who was among those rescued, broke down in tears while recounting his ordeal.
He said traffickers had held him captive in a makeshift hut in the hills for eight days. Despite attempting to escape twice, he failed. A group of 40 to 50 armed men guarded the hideout, he added.
Asaduzzaman said he had become acquainted with Imamul, a Rohingya imam from the Kutupalong camp in Ukhiya, while working on a bridge in Cox’s Bazar. They later developed a relationship.
Imamul eventually lured him with the promise of a job at the camp and called him there eight days ago. His mobile phone and other belongings were confiscated before he was taken to the hills in a CNG-run auto-rickshaw at night and handed over to the traffickers.
At the hideout, he found more than 50 other people being held captive. That was when he realised he had fallen into a human trafficking gang’s trap, he said.
He added that a trawler was being prepared for a sea voyage two days earlier, with more than 100 people expected to be transported by boat. The traffickers tried to take him and five others to the trawler, but they were left behind due to a lack of space.
"We were scheduled to be trafficked yesterday. Fortunately, the army arrived and rescued us. But it is heartbreaking that a patriotic army soldier lost his life while rescuing us," he said.
Saiful and Mizanur Rahman Sagar, residents of Sebatkhal in Ukhiya who were among those rescued, said a broker named Nurali had handed them over to the traffickers on the promise of jobs.
They later learned from the traffickers that the two of them had been bought for Tk1 lakh, they alleged.
"For five days, we saw four to five new people being brought to the hideout every day. Anyone who tried to speak up was brutally beaten. We were also beaten when we attempted to escape. Later, they tied us up with iron chains," they said.
They added that they were given food only twice a day, consisting of raw pumpkin and lentils, leaving them severely hungry.
"We were supposed to be put on a trawler and trafficked by sea on Thursday. The joint forces rescued us just in time. There was heavy gunfire during the operation. It felt as though a war was going on in the hills," they said.
Nur Alam, a resident of Hnila, said a sweeping operation was essential to dismantle the powerful network of human traffickers.
"Gunshots can be heard in the hills almost every day. Armed traffickers have made the entire area unsafe. Their hideouts have spread across the hills of Baharchhara, Hnila and Whykong. There is no alternative to a coordinated operation to dismantle these hideouts," he said.
Mohammad Ali, acting chairman of Hnila Union Parishad, said the activities of armed groups operating in the hills were increasing day by day, with human traffickers becoming particularly active during the winter season.
"An army soldier was killed in a gunfight at a traffickers' hideout yesterday. What could be more alarming than this? Ordinary people here are virtually helpless in the face of these criminals.
A sweeping operation in the hills is urgently needed to bring the situation under control," he said. Teknaf Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) SM Anik Chowdhury said law enforcement agencies were working to arrest the armed human traffickers operating in the hills.
"No one will be allowed to escape justice after committing a crime. We are also monitoring the planned human chains," he said.
Expressing deep sorrow over the death of the army soldier, the UNO said eliminating such criminal activities required collective cooperation from local residents alongside efforts by law enforcement agencies.

item.title: Salahuddin: People won’t allow AL to engage in politics again
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Friday ruled out the possibility of Awami League's return to politics, saying the people would never again allow the party, which he described as oppressive, autocratic, fascist and murderous, to engage in politics in the country.
"Those who shed people's blood to establish fascism, oppressed the people and committed genocide will have no place in the country's politics again," he said while addressing the concluding session of the 104th two-day annual religious conference at Al-Jamiatul Islamiah Azizul Uloom Babunagar in Fatikchhari, Chittagong.
Questioning whether the people wanted the return of those he described as fascist forces, the minister said some were trying to create conditions for their comeback.
"Those who were forced to flee the country in the face of the mass uprising will not be allowed to return and engage in politics here," he said, adding that those responsible for mass killings and repression had yet to express regret or remorse.
Salahuddin said people were united in opposing the political activities of those responsible for mass killings, despite their differences in political views and ideologies.
He also alleged that fascist forces were behind attempts to create unrest in the garment sector.
Addressing those who were creating trouble in the name of movements, the minister urged them to engage in constructive criticism. "You may choose not to cooperate with the government, but do not withhold your cooperation from the people of this country," he said.
He said it had taken 16 to 17 years to free the country from what he described as an autocratic and Islam-hostile regime.
Salahuddin said many Islamic scholars and students had sacrificed their lives during the struggle.
Citing United Nations estimates, he said around 1,400 people had been killed during the July-August mass uprising, adding that nearly 3,000 people had been victims of enforced disappearance during the preceding 16 to 17 years.
"I was also one of them. By the grace of Almighty Allah and through people's prayers, I am still alive," the minister said.
He claimed that around 7,000 people had been killed or subjected to various forms of torture and persecution during that period, while millions had faced harassment through attacks and cases.
Salahuddin said they wanted the country to prosper economically and improve the living standards of Islamic scholars (ulema) and students of Qawmi madrasahs.
He also alleged that some groups use the name of Islam for political gain, although their election manifestos contain no mention of Islamic values. “Although they say one thing, their documents and official records tell a different story,” he said.
"We believe in Islamic values. We are the party that included 'Bismillah' in the Constitution. We follow the nationalist and Islamic values introduced by Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman," the minister said.
"We have built a united Bangladesh where people from all walks of life share a common national identity. We never want to see division among the people of this country," he added.

item.title: BRAC, UNESCO sign agreement to develop creative economy roadmap
item.description:
Efforts to strengthen Bangladesh's creative economy have gained momentum with a new partnership focusing on film, cultural tourism and heritage, as BRAC and the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to advance the country's creative sectors.
Asif Saleh, executive director of BRAC, and Susan Vize, head of office and UNESCO representative to Bangladesh, signed the agreement at BRAC Centre in Dhaka on Thursday.
Asif Saleh said: “Bangladesh's culture and heritage – our crafts, music, film and living traditions – are an economic asset we have only begun to tap. This agreement with UNESCO is about changing that: bringing together the evidence and ideas to support the government to build its national strategy and roadmap for a creative economy that creates real jobs, including for the many people already working in it informally.
“At BRAC, we see this as one interconnected ecosystem. Through Aarong's decades of work with artisans, our long-running popular theatre program and our community-based tourism initiative Otithi, we look forward to working with UNESCO, the private sector and others to help the sector grow.”
Susan Vize said: “Bangladesh has a wealth of cultural heritage and creativity that can be harnessed to improve the lives of everyday Bangladeshis from craftspeople to dancers to chefs. We believe this partnership can help identify key pathways to build on this foundation.”
The partnership will support the development of a national roadmap for the creative economy, identifying priorities and practical steps for growth in the short, medium and long term. It will also assess Bangladesh’s existing creative ecosystem to identify opportunities, address gaps and strengthen collaboration among key stakeholders.
The initiative will focus particularly on the film and audio-visual industries, cultural and community-based tourism, film festivals and heritage.
The collaboration will also explore the establishment of a national Creative Cities Network to help cities build on their cultural heritage and creative strengths.
As part of this effort, BRAC and UNESCO will examine the possibility of Dhaka joining UNESCO’s Creative Cities Network, which brings together cities that use creativity and cultural industries to support sustainable urban development.
Through the partnership, BRAC and UNESCO aim to strengthen Bangladesh’s creative industries, expand economic opportunities and livelihoods, and safeguard and promote the country’s cultural heritage.
Also present at the event were KAM Morshed, senior director of advocacy, communications and engagement at BRAC; Moutushi Kabir, chief people and culture officer of BRAC; and Kizzy Tahnin, head of culture at the UNESCO Dhaka Office.

item.title: Mahdi Amin: Cybersecurity at individual, institutional levels key govt priority
item.description:
Prime Minister's Adviser on Education and Primary and Mass Education Mahdi Amin has said ensuring effective cybersecurity at both individual and institutional levels is one of the key priorities of the government.
The government is working to implement policies and legal frameworks that would protect every citizen, safeguard the privacy of personal information, and ensure everyone's dignity and online security, he said.
Mahdi outlined the government plans while speaking as chief guest at the “CyberFrames National Award” ceremony held at North South University in the capital on Thursday night.
Highlighting the importance of cybersecurity, the adviser said people are constantly falling victim to cyber fraud, financial irregularities, disinformation and misinformation.
He said false information is being used to create confusion and commit crimes such as character assassination. The digital platform is also being used to harass women and make them feel unsafe.
He said a strong national consensus could be reached through open consultations and dialogue, while upholding the core objectives of cybersecurity.
Mahdi Amin said the North South University, country's first private university, was established on the basis of policies formulated through the visionary thinking of the BNP government and then Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia.
Recalling the courageous contributions of the university's teachers and students during the 2024 July Mass Uprising, he said the government will take all necessary measures to further strengthen private universities.
North South University Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Abdul Hannan Chowdhury addressed the program virtually.
Among others, North South University Board of Trustees member and Acting Chairman M A Kashem, member Benazir Ahmed and Pro-Vice-Chancellor Professor Nasar U Ahmed attended the event.

item.title: RMG production set to return to normal from Sunday
item.description:
The country’s garment industry is expected to return to full-scale production from Sunday after several days of worker unrest, protests and disruptions, with factory owners hoping that October wage payments will help restore a normal working environment.
The situation improved significantly on Friday across industrial areas in Savar, Ashulia, Gazipur, Mirpur and Narayanganj. In Savar and Ashulia, workers returned to their jobs peacefully at 88 garment factories, while road protests, clashes and tensions declined compared with previous days.
However, production has yet to return to normal at some factories.
Factory owners said the 88 factories in Ashulia remained open on Friday, despite the weekly holiday, to meet urgent shipment deadlines. Garment factories will remain closed on Saturday in line with the public holiday marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day.
Preparations are now underway to resume regular production from Sunday.
Several industry owners said they would seek to maximise output to make up for losses in production and deliveries caused by the recent unrest. They are also prioritising workers’ return and maintaining a stable working environment.
Owners expect the payment of October wages on Sunday to further ease tensions. They said workers were generally less likely to stage protests or work stoppages on payday, raising hopes that production would continue without disruption.

item.title: APBn member brutally beaten in Rupganj over anti-drug stance
item.description:
An Armed Police Battalion (APBn) member was allegedly lured to an isolated area and brutally assaulted by suspected drug traders in Rupganj, Narayanganj, for speaking out against drug activities.
The attackers allegedly beat Abul Kalam with sticks and locally made weapons, breaking his arms and legs and severing a tendon in one of his legs. He is now undergoing treatment at the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopaedic Rehabilitation (NITOR) in Dhaka.
The attack took place around 11pm on Thursday in the North Masabo area of Tarabo Municipality.
Kalam had reportedly been opposing drug-related activities in the area for a long time and faced threats for helping law enforcers bring suspected drug traders to justice.
A few days ago, he helped police arrest two alleged drug traders, identified as Shahadat and Emdadul. Following the arrests, Shahadat’s younger brother, Shahjalal, allegedly threatened Kalam several times over the phone and in person.
According to the allegations, Shahjalal called Kalam around 11pm on Thursday, saying he needed to discuss something urgent. He then took him towards an isolated wetland near his home, where 10–15 people were waiting.
The group attacked Kalam as soon as he arrived, beating him repeatedly and allegedly breaking his limbs with sticks and locally made weapons. They also allegedly cut a tendon in his leg.
Hearing his cries, local residents rushed towards the scene, prompting the attackers to flee. They rescued Kalam and took him to a nearby private hospital. He was later referred to NITOR as his condition was serious.
Rupganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge AHM Salahuddin said he had heard about the incident but had not received a written complaint. Police would take legal action after investigating if a complaint was filed.

item.title: Hasan six-for puts Bangladesh back in contention
item.description:
Fast bowler Hasan Mahmud claimed 6-90 as Bangladesh fought back strongly to leave the second and final cricket Test against West Indies evenly poised at Sylhet International Cricket Stadium today.
Hasan's superb bowling helped Bangladesh dismiss West Indies for 356 after the visitors had looked set for a much bigger total.
The hosts, however, suffered yet another top-order collapse, which is increasingly becoming a recurring problem. Mushfiqur Rahim and Towhid Hridoy then combined to steady the innings, guiding Bangladesh to 85-3 before bad light forced an early close.
Hridoy was unbeaten on 29, while Mushfiqur was batting on 19 when the umpires called off play.
Nayeem Hasan came in as a makeshift opener after Shadman Islam suffered an ankle injury. However, he failed to withstand an aggressive spell from the West Indies pacers and fell for 5, caught by Brandon King at first slip off Jayden Seales.
Justin Greaves then cut short Tanzid Hasan Tamim's stay at the crease, dismissing him for 16 after debutant Kevin Wickham held on to a stunning catch at cover point.
Shamar Joseph subsequently rattled the stumps of Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto, who was beaten by the swing, for 18, leaving Bangladesh at 51-3.
Mushfiqur Rahim and Towhid Hridoy, however, managed to weather the West Indies attack before bad light interrupted the proceeding.
Resuming the day at 235-4, West Indies initially appeared poised to take complete control of the match. But Hasan turned the game around with a double strike. He first bowled Amir Jangoo for 133, ending a 106-run partnership between Jangoo and Justin Greaves. Jangoo added 22 runs to his overnight score before departing.
Hasan then dismissed West Indies captain Roston Chase for a duck with the very next delivery to put himself on a hat-trick.
He appeared to have completed the hat-trick when he trapped Joshua Bishop leg-before, but Bishop successfully reviewed the decision to overturn the on-field call.
Hasan's accuracy and consistency, however, continued to trouble the visitors. He eventually dismissed Bishop for 23 to complete his fifth five-wicket haul in Test cricket.
Greaves, meanwhile, weathered the Bangladesh pace attack and helped West Indies cross the 300-run mark, completing his half-century in the process.
Mehidy Hasan Miraz finally broke Greaves' resistance, dismissing him for 51 to give Bangladesh their first success through spin.
Hasan then claimed his second six-wicket haul in Test cricket by removing Shamar Joseph before Miraz dismissed Jayden Seales to wrap up the West Indies innings.

item.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted drone in Mecca region
item.description:
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said on Friday it had intercepted a drone in the region of Mecca, Islam’s holiest city, following repeated attacks on the kingdom by the pro-Iran group.
“Interception and destruction of a drone in the Mecca region,” Turki al-Malki, the coalition’s spokesman, wrote on social media, without elaborating on the source of the attack.
Since the breakdown of a truce in July, Saudi Arabia has traded blows with the Houthis, who have struck Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and military sites.
But the group has repeatedly said their forces will not target the holy cities of Mecca or Medina.
On Thursday, the Saudi coalition said it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis at the Medina region, a claim denounced by the group as “blatant and grave falsehood.”
On the ground in Yemen, the Houthis have also been fighting forces from the country’s Saudi-backed internationally recognized government.
A September offensive saw the Houthis capture areas overlooking the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, which links Europe to Asia via the Red Sea and Suez Canal.
Government forces have since been trying to retake territory, backed by Saudi air power.

item.title: US pro-Trump election deniers crash against ‘blue tsunami’
item.description:
For months, conspiracy-peddling supporters of President Donald Trump spread baseless theories that the vote would be rigged. But those claims all but dried up after Democrats swept the US midterm elections.
Political pundits had anticipated a wave of legal challenges from election deniers seeking to contest the results of Tuesday’s vote, or efforts by Trump himself to tilt the outcome in his favor -- as he did when he tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat.
But none of that materialized.
And evidence-free claims of fraud slowed to a trickle after what observers called the decisive “blue tsunami” of Democratic victories that handed the party control of both chambers of Congress.
Trump’s acceptance of the results, signaling he would not challenge his Republican Party’s sweeping defeat, set the tone for many of his loyalists to follow suit.
“Election day 2026 featured a few rumors about election integrity. However, election denialism was not a core narrative used to explain the sweeping victories by Democrats once they became apparent,” said the University of Washington’s Center for an Informed Public.
“Absent a political elite to champion election denialism, rumoring about election integrity has not coalesced into a coherent or significant narrative to explain election results.”
Many analysts said the scale of the Democratic victory -- widely seen as a repudiation of Trump’s political agenda -- may have played a role.
However, David Becker, executive director of the nonpartisan Center for Election Innovation and Research, argued that fraud claims persisted in the past even when the president’s preferred candidates lost by large margins.
“I don’t know necessarily that margin of victory makes much difference to those who have profited off of the economy of grift around election conspiracies for quite some time,” Becker said.
“It might be that politics overall in the nation have changed to some degree, and that creates a different incentive structure.”
It also did not help that many election deniers on the ballot lost their races -- and chose not to challenge the results.
Among them was Andy Biggs, one of the Republican politicians who joined Trump in challenging the 2020 election results after his defeat to Joe Biden.
After losing Arizona’s gubernatorial race, Biggs conceded to incumbent Democrat Katie Hobbs, making no mention of voter fraud and instead blaming what he perceived as a low voter turnout.
“We just didn’t get our turnout quite as full as we wanted to,” he said in comments reported by US media.
Even conservative influencers -- including prominent supporters of Trump’s Make America Great Again (Maga) movement who have been vocal election skeptics -- appeared subdued.
Ahead of the midterm elections, some skeptics went so far as to call for a “national emergency,” urging Trump to grant himself “king-like powers” over the midterms, according to the left-leaning watchdog Media Matters for America.
“I have been banging the drum of rigged and stolen elections since 2020, but that is not why we lost the midterms,” conservative political commentator Rogan O’Handley wrote to his 2.3 million followers on X.
“We lost because we failed to fix the things voters sent us to do... Lower gas and food prices and stop the Iran war.”
Media Matters’s John Knefel cautioned against “premature” hopes that “the election denial fever has permanently broken.”
“Rejecting Democratic Party wins remains a core, foundational element of the movement that Trump built and will likely continue to be one for the foreseeable future,” he said.
But striking a note of optimism, Becker said “American voters are tired” of evidence-free election denialism.
“A smaller number of election skeptics ran this time than in past cycles, and there seem to be substantially less stomach for these claims among voters,” said Pamela Smith, president of the nonpartisan nonprofit Verified Voting.
Citing an independent poll, Smith added: “Most voters are interested in other issues -- fraud in elections does not seem to be a driver for deciding their vote.”

item.title: Nato seeks ‘just’ end to Ukraine war as Trump touts deal involving Europe
item.description:
Ukraine’s allies are working for a “just and sustainable” end to the war ahead of US-mediated talks next week in Abu Dhabi, Nato said Friday, after US President Donald Trump touted a deal with Russia involving “all of Europe.”
Talks in Brussels on Thursday involving Nato, US, Ukrainian and European officials “built on productive discussions in Miami and Oslo and sought to advance a just and sustainable end to the war in Ukraine,” an alliance spokeswoman said.
Trump on Thursday predicted a “very big” deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but “all of Europe,” in remarks that will fuel fears on the continent of a pivot towards the Kremlin.
Jared Kushner, the president’s envoy and son-in-law, said the United States was working on “a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace.”
Kushner, who participated in the Brussels talks via video link, said that Washington’s “objective is to develop practical arrangements that address the security concerns of all sides.”
“We are exploring five principal goals: permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term European security and stability,” he posted online.
He insisted that “any arrangements must fully respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and independent decision-making of every nation” and said Nato would “remain central to European collective defense.”
The US push will rattle Washington’s European allies, who have long rejected Moscow’s desire to rewrite the European security architecture.
Before launching the war in Ukraine in 2022, the Kremlin delivered an ultimatum to Nato which included a demand that the alliance’s troops be withdrawn from eastern Europe.
That was rejected by the Western military alliance.
Europe has meanwhile been seeking to play a bigger role in the US-led push to end the fighting.
Kushner said that Washington will “consult closely with our European partners on the sidelines” of the Abu Dhabi talks and “if progress is made, aim to move toward a broader multilateral format with their direct participation.”

item.title: Rashed Khan accuses Jamaat of double standards in bid for power
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Political Affairs Assistant Rashed Khan has strongly criticised Jamaat-e-Islami Bangladesh’s political strategy, accusing the party of misleading the public and deceiving its alliance partners.
He also criticised the successive resignations of several key leaders from the National Citizen Party (NCP), saying the developments had exposed contradictions in Jamaat’s politics.
He made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists after offering Juma prayers at Pagla Kanai Sayadatiya Jame Mosque in Jhenaidah town on Friday.
Commenting on the recent resignations of several female leaders from the NCP, Rashed said Nahid Islam’s biggest failure was his inability to retain leaders like Samanta Shermeen in the party.
“Many of those who joined the NCP with certain aspirations are now leaving the party one after another,” he said.
He further said Nasiruddin Patwary had earlier accused Jamaat of not wanting reforms and engaging in hypocrisy in the name of reforms. Samanta Shermeen had raised similar allegations before resigning, he added.
“This shows how true these allegations are,” Rashed said.
Criticising Jamaat’s politics, he said the party was using Islam as a political tool to mislead people in Bangladesh.
“In meetings with foreigners, they claim that they have not talked about introducing Sharia law if they come to power, but their constitution clearly mentions it,” he said.
Questioning Jamaat’s understanding with its alliance partners, Rashed said Colonel Oli Ahmed had publicly stated at a rally that Jamaat’s ameer had assured him that if the 11-party alliance came to power, the country would be governed under existing laws and the constitution, not Shariah law.
“This makes it clear that Jamaat is deceiving the people of Bangladesh as well as its own alliance partners,” he said.
BNP leaders KM Wazed, former Pagla Kanai Union Parishad chairman Nazrul Islam and former convenor of Islami University Chhatra Dal Shahed Ahmed, among others, were present at the event.

item.title: IUB, Prime Bank Investment sign MoU to promote financial literacy
item.description:
Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB) and Prime Bank Investment PLC (PBIL) signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on November 2, 2026, to promote financial literacy, strengthen industry-academia collaboration and create practical learning opportunities for students.
The agreement was signed by IUB Vice Chancellor Prof M Tamim and Prime Bank Investment PLC Managing Director and CEO Syed M Omar Tayub at the Vice Chancellor's Lounge.
Under the partnership, the institutions will jointly implement “PrimeInvest Youth: Invest for Tomorrow,” an initiative aimed at increasing students’ investment awareness and understanding of financial markets.
A key component of the initiative is a one-day internship program that will provide selected IUB students with practical exposure to portfolio management, investment research, capital market operations and financial advisory.
The partnership will also facilitate workshops, seminars and knowledge-sharing sessions on savings, investment, portfolio diversification, tax planning and risk management for students, faculty members and employees.
The Prime Bank Investment delegation included Md Shiful Islam, Head of Wealth, Advisory and Research; Md Abdullah Al Nahid, Deputy Head of Portfolio Management Department; Rupa Roy, Team Leader and Senior Relationship Manager of the Portfolio Management Department; and Md Mazharul Islam, Manager of Brand, Marketing and Partnership.
Representing IUB, Dr Ikramul Hasan, Dean (Acting) of the School of Business and Entrepreneurship, attended the program along with several faculty members from the Department of Finance and other departments of the school.

item.title: Mukesh Rishi set for Dhallywood debut in ‘Naseeb’
item.description:
Indian actor Mukesh Rishi is set to make his debut in Bangladeshi cinema with director Mohammad Iqbal’s upcoming film “Naseeb”, in which he will play the main antagonist.
Iqbal confirmed that Rishi is expected to arrive in Bangladesh later this month to join the shooting. The actor will also appear in several major action sequences.
The first phase of filming has been completed at different locations in Cox’s Bazar. The production team is preparing for the second schedule in Bogura, where shooting is scheduled to begin on November 9.
Rishi is known for playing villains in Hindi films opposite leading actors including Amitabh Bachchan, Salman Khan and Aamir Khan. Active in the Indian film industry since the 1990s, he has also appeared in Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam and Punjabi productions.
His Bollywood credits include “Sooryavansham”, “Lal Baadshah” and “Kohram” with Bachchan, as well as “Judwaa”, “Bandhan” and “Garv: Pride and Honour” with Khan.
“Naseeb” will mark Rishi’s first appearance in a Bangladeshi film.

item.title: Bangladeshi films ‘Roid’ and ‘Delupi’ win awards in Barcelona
item.description:
Two Bangladeshi films, “Roid” and “Delupi”, have received awards at the Asian Film Festival Barcelona in Spain, adding to their growing international recognition.
Directed by Mejbaur Rahman Sumon, “Roid” won Best Film in the festival’s Official Selection section, while Mohammad Touqir Islam’s “Delupi” received a special mention in the Other Narrative section.
The cast and crew of “Roid” welcomed the recognition. The film previously won awards for Best Actress, Best Cinematography and Best Music at Canada’s Mosaic International Film Festival. It has also been selected to represent Bangladesh at the 99th Academy Awards.
“Roid” follows Sadu and his wife, Pagli, exploring their relationship through love, silence and everyday experiences. Mostafizur Noor Imran and Nazifa Tushi play the central roles.
The film began its international festival run at the International Film Festival Rotterdam in the Netherlands earlier this year before its theatrical release in Bangladesh during Eid-ul-Azha.
The Barcelona recognition marks another international achievement for “Delupi”, which has participated in 10 overseas film festivals. Earlier, cast member Chiranjeet Biswas won Best Actor at the Tasveer Film Festival in North America.
Released in Bangladesh last year, “Delupi” explores the lives and experiences of people in the country's southern region. Its narrative brings together politics, relationships, natural disasters, the struggles of jatra performers and the search for change.
All members of the cast are residents of Khulna. Before “Delupi”, director Touqir received recognition for his work on the series “Shaaticup” and “Sinpaat”.

item.title: Robert Pattinson named recipient of 40th American Cinematheque Award
item.description:
Hollywood actor Robert Pattinson has been selected to receive the 40th American Cinematheque Award in recognition of his two-decade career and work across independent films and major studio productions.
Pattinson will receive the honour at a ceremony on February 9, 2027, at the Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills, California.
American Cinematheque board chair Rick Nicita praised the actor for his dedication to his craft, creative choices and versatility. He also highlighted Pattinson’s collaborations with acclaimed filmmakers and his ability to connect with audiences through blockbuster productions.
Pattinson first gained international recognition through the “Twilight” franchise. He has since built a diverse filmography with projects including “Good Time”, “The Lighthouse”, “The Batman” and “Mickey 17”.
His career has included collaborations with filmmakers known for distinctive storytelling, while his choice of challenging and unconventional roles has helped establish his reputation as a versatile performer.
The American Cinematheque Award is presented annually to an artiste whose contributions to the film industry merit special recognition.

item.title: ‘Off Campus’ season two sets April 2027 premiere date
item.description:
Prime Video has announced that the second season of its college drama “Off Campus” will premiere on April 28, 2027, with several cast members returning for the new instalment.
The announcement comes less than a year after the first season debuted on May 13. The series received an early renewal in February, before its premiere, allowing production on the second season to move forward on a shorter timeline.
Created by Louisa Levy and based on Elle Kennedy’s bestselling “Off-Campus” book series, the show follows an elite college ice hockey team and the women in their lives as they navigate romance, friendship and the challenges of adulthood.
According to the report, the first season attracted 36 million viewers in its first 12 days, becoming the third most-watched debut season in Prime Video history. It also recorded the platform’s most-watched debut among women aged 18–34 and remained in the streamer’s global Top 10 six months after its release.
The second season will focus on the relationship between Allie Hayes, played by Mika Abdalla, and Dean Di Laurentis, portrayed by Stephen Kalyn. Their storyline is based on “The Mistake”, the second novel in Kennedy’s series.
Returning cast members include Belmont Cameli as Garrett Graham, Ella Bright as Hannah Wells, Antonio Cipriano as John Logan and Jalen Thomas Brooks as John Tucker. Josh Heuston, whose character's storyline concluded in the first season, will not return.
India Fowler joins the main cast as Grace Ivers, John Logan’s romantic interest. Returning recurring cast members include Julia Sarah Stone as Jules, Khobe Clarke as Beau Maxwell and Miles Gutierrez-Riley as Dexter.
Philipa Soo will also appear in a recurring role as Scarlett, a theatre artist invited to guest-direct an original production in the college’s drama department.
The new season will continue adapting Kennedy’s interconnected stories set in the Briar University community, with a new central romance and returning characters.
